references.text: The land became unclean, and God punished it for its sin, so that the land vomited out its inhabitants. This verse explains why the land reacts to sin.
A parallel warning to keep God's laws so that the land will not spit out the Israelites, using the same imagery of the land's reaction to sin.
Moses explains that it is not because of Israel's righteousness that they receive the land, but because of the wickedness of the nations who lived there before them.
The warning that Israel will be uprooted from the land if they are disobedient, a parallel consequence to being spat out.
Joshua's warning to Israel that they will perish from the good land if they break the covenant and serve other gods.
The description of how the Israelites sinned like the nations before them and were led away from the land, fulfilling the warning in Leviticus.
Ezekiel uses similar language about the land 'devouring' people because of sin.
Ezra refers to how the land became unclean due to the abominable deeds of the peoples, and that Israel should not mix with them.
